scenes.headline: How a 2-bit model learns new scales
scenes.sub: Same codes, retuned scales, under 8 GB
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Whippet! Saluki fits a twenty-seven billion parameter model in under eight gigabytes. Let's see what was actually changed.

scenes.label: The idea
scenes.text: Start from a strong 2-bit file, keep every code it chose, and retrain only the small scales around them, aimed at tool calls.
scenes.say: Start from a good two-bit file, keep every code it chose, and retrain only the scales around them.

scenes.title: One block of 256 weights
scenes.say: Every block of two hundred fifty-six weights is stored the same way.

parts.note: a fixed grid point, picked by the code
parts.say: Each code picks a point on a fixed grid. That choice is most of the file.
One sixteen-bit scale stretches the whole block.

parts.note: the weight the model actually uses
parts.say: Change the scale, and the whole block moves, without touching a code.

scenes.title: From the full model to Saluki

steps.say: It starts with the full model. A research lab learned which grid point every weight should land on.
A search then gave each tensor its own number of bits, under a size budget. That file is the base.
Underdog pushed a few dozen feed-forward tensors to the cheapest two-bit type, to get under eight gigabytes.
Then it trained the block scales, norms and a few gates, with the codes frozen.

left.title: Re-quantized
left.say: Comparing the two files byte by byte, a few tensors were re-quantized from scratch.

right.title: Same codes
right.say: Everywhere else, the codes match exactly. Only the two-byte scale in each block moved, by about one percent.

steps.say: On Underdog's tool-calling test, the base file passes seventy-six tasks.
With the same codes and retuned scales, Saluki passes eighty-eight. The full model passes eighty-four: a tie at this sample size.

scenes.text: A 2-bit file's scales are a thin layer you can retrain for a task, without leaving the stock format.
scenes.mark: a thin layer you can retrain
scenes.say: The scales in a two-bit file are a thin layer you can retrain for a task, and it still loads in stock llama.cpp.

recap: Ties the full model on tool calls
scenes.say: Built on a lab's two-bit file. Codes frozen, scales retuned. A tie with the full model on tool calls, and weaker at math.
